column1: # slice-reinterpret.tsv — detector D1 allowlist (kills Bun regression Class 1, oven-sh/bun#31188).
# Generated: 2026-07-12
# Gate: .port/tools/gates/check_slice_reinterpret.sh
# Oracle: /Users/gael/projects/ghostty pinned @ 6ad1fe7d8 (every zig_origin resolves against this pin).
#   (was 4749c4e9; the two page_impl.rs rows were re-audited against the new pin on 2026-07-31 —
#    both @ptrCast sites still exist upstream, only their line numbers moved.)
# WHY THIS AUDIT EXISTS (Bun Class 1):
#   Zig's `bun.reinterpretSlice(u16, buf)` / `@as([]T, @ptrCast(x))` silently @divTrunc
#   the trailing bytes that don't fill a whole element; the naive Rust twin
#   (`bytemuck::cast_slice`) PANICS on the same slop instead. The escaped defect
#   (#31188, odd-length UTF-16 Blob) shipped past every Bun gate because Miri sees
#   only *misalignment* UB — never the truncate-vs-panic *semantic* divergence.
#   So each slice reinterpret in the port carries an EXPLICIT decision here, and the
#   gate FAILS on any reinterpret hit that is not on this allowlist (fail-closed).
# SCAN (the gate greps crates/ + crates-sys/ for, verbatim):
#   bytemuck::cast_slice | align_to | from_raw_parts.*as *(const|mut) u(16|32|64)
#   | bytes_of | cast_slice_mut
#   (u8 reinterprets are excluded by construction: element size 1 => no truncation
#   possible, byte-identity. The pattern targets only widening to u16/u32/u64.)
# SCHEMA (5 tab-separated columns; comment lines start with '#'; blank lines ignored):
#   1 site           <repo-relative-file>:<line> of the reinterpret (must currently match a scan hit)
#   2 decision       one of: truncate | error | exact-len-proven
#                       truncate         = Zig @divTrunc semantics deliberately reproduced
#                                          (e.g. `&buf[..buf.len() & !1]`); MUST name an
#                                          odd/misaligned-length test in column 4.
#                       error            = the port rejects non-exact length (panic/Err);
#                                          MUST name an odd/misaligned-length test in column 4.
#                       exact-len-proven = the byte length is provably an exact multiple of
#                                          the target element size at this site (same-count
#                                          reinterpret over a size-locked element, or a
#                                          compile-time-literal length matching the alloc), so
#                                          NO odd-length path exists; column 4 names the layout/
#                                          length proof test instead.
#   3 zig_origin     the ghostty line this ports (path:line + the reinterpret expression)
#   4 test           name of the guarding #[test] (odd/misaligned for truncate|error; layout/
#                    length proof for exact-len-proven)
#   5 notes          the proof / rationale
site
crates/rustty-vt/src/page_impl.rs:1786
column5: RE-AUDITED 2026-07-31 (line drift 1779->1786 from 9d8fafb/389dde0/f79d83a, which inserted code ABOVE this site; the reinterpret expression itself is byte-identical and the zig origin moved 1122->1142 with the oracle pin bump 4749c4e93->6ad1fe7d8, unchanged in substance). Cell is `#[repr(transparent)] struct Cell(u64)`; size_of::<Cell>()==8==size_of::<u64>() (cell_layout_size_align asserts 8/8). The reinterpret passes `len` (the CELL count) as the u64 count, so len cells == len u64s byte-for-byte — no slop is representable. Faithful to Zig @ptrCast slice, whose recomputed len is identical because @sizeOf(Cell)==@sizeOf(u64).
